held_tables.qualification: The 11,011 rows are an author-published, curated reaction-structure dataset, rather than a private or unavailable Reaxys dump. Goodman and Lam (2024) explicitly used the original Li/Tang (2022) training reactions, published the processed file, and described its filtering in the supporting information. The original 2022 paper explicitly publishes the training/validation repository in its Data Availability statement and carries a CC BY-NC 3.0 article notice. All 11,011 local rows exactly match the Goodman source. An independent structure join matches 11,009 original training records; two rows retain connectivity and product identity but differ in reactant stereochemical notation. Public availability and article licensing are therefore established. However, an explicit downstream grant for these external reaction files, or the applicable author/Elsevier agreement covering redistribution of the extracted reaction compilation, has not been located. The original repository MIT notice refers to software and documentation and retains another project copyright; the Goodman repository has no dataset-specific licence file. Reaxys publishing guidance from 2022 expressly permits some publications and unlimited substance identifiers/SMILES, so Reaxys provenance alone does not establish prohibition. It does not clearly cover republishing 11,011 paired reactant-product reaction records. The status remains an unresolved redistribution-grant scope under the project verified-grant gate; it is not a finding that authors or future reuse are prohibited.

remaining_qualification: Article publication and public author deposit are verified and should be stated positively. Noncommercial publication is acceptable to this project; the CC BY-NC condition alone is not the reason for this hold.

The 2022 Reaxys guidance is guidance only, subject to change, and describes collaboration work products. The specific author agreement or an explicit permission exception was not available for review; no contrary inference about author compliance is made.

The unlimited Reaxys identifiers passage includes substance structures as SMILES. This is not an unambiguous grant for a large compilation of paired reaction transformations; individual facts or structures and compilation or database rights must not be conflated.

The current RSC CC BY-NC example agreement, version 8.2 clause 2.10, excludes raw research data from the article publishing agreement. It is current scope guidance, rather than proof of the signed 2022 author agreement or a retroactive change to an existing grant.
This decision concerns mirroring the complete 11,011-row payload in a release. It does not prohibit citing the original public deposits or preserving a reproducible source-download recipe.
No author or Elsevier contact has been made. No original dataset or previously pinned source was changed.
